title: Downsample sensor readings from any kind of list

blocks.text: The monitoring charts can't draw millions of points, so `Downsampler` keeps every `step`-th sensor reading: positions 0, `step`, 2·`step`, and so on. Two callers use it. The live dashboard passes buffers of four million readings and keeps one in a thousand. The archive job passes readings it replays from disk into a linked list, and keeps one in seven. The first version was correct on both, and the archive job ran for hours; the second fixed the archive job, and the dashboard started reading every reading in the buffer to keep a thousandth of them.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Downsampler.java`: `pick(readings, step)` returns the kept readings in order, and stays fast for both callers, and for any other `List` that reaches it. About eight lines.
The tests count the links a linked list walks, and the readings a buffer is asked for.

cases.says: the readings at positions 0, step, 2·step and so on are kept, in order, from array-backed, linked and immutable lists
a short list of replayed readings is sampled correctly
sampling a linked list walks its links about once, not once per kept reading
sampling a list with fast random access reads only the readings it keeps

origin.section: An Abstraction Hides Its Cost Too: List.get(i) Is O(n) on a LinkedList

concepts: List does not promise what get(i) costs: it walks the links on a LinkedList, so code over any List iterates, and uses indexes only on a RandomAccess list.
